about: Draft claims for section 2 of the Q1 paper (DLV-05). Each is checked by a reader who did not write it.

claims.ref: Spirtes, Glymour, Scheines. Causation, Prediction, and Search, 2nd ed., MIT Press, 2000
claims.claim: Constraint-based algorithms such as PC and FCI recover causal structure from conditional-independence tests only up to an equivalence class, and only under assumptions such as faithfulness (and, for PC, causal sufficiency); FCI drops causal sufficiency and outputs a partial ancestral graph.

claims.ref: Chickering. Optimal structure identification with greedy search. JMLR 3, 2002
claims.claim: Greedy Equivalence Search (GES) searches over Markov equivalence classes with a score and is consistent in the large-sample limit.

claims.ref: Reisach, Seiler, Weichwald. Beware of the Simulated DAG! Causal Discovery Benchmarks May Be Easy To Game. NeurIPS 2021 (arXiv 2102.13647)
claims.claim: In commonly used simulated benchmarks the marginal variance tends to increase along the causal order (varsortability), so a baseline that sorts variables by variance and regresses matches continuous-optimisation methods on raw data, while those methods fail after standardisation.

claims.ref: Reisach, Tami, Seiler, Chambaz, Weichwald. A Scale-Invariant Sorting Criterion to Find a Causal Order in Additive Noise Models. NeurIPS 2023 (arXiv 2303.18211)
claims.claim: A scale-invariant analogue, R2-sortability (sorting by the coefficient of determination), is also high in default simulation settings and can be exploited by a simple baseline.

claims.ref: Kitson, Constantinou. The impact of variable ordering on Bayesian network structure learning. Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery 2024 (arXiv 2206.08952)
claims.claim: The order of the columns in the input file alone changes the graph that score-based hill climbing learns, by more than a large increase in sample size does.

claims.ref: Brouillard, Squires, Wahl, Kording, Sachs, Drouin, Sridhar. The Landscape of Causal Discovery Data: Grounding Causal Discovery in Real-World Applications. CLeaR 2025 (arXiv 2412.01953)
claims.claim: A review of causal-discovery papers finds that the Sachs protein-signalling data is the only real dataset in a large share of real-data evaluations, that its ground truth is not definitive, and recommends evaluation on interventional data.

claims.ref: Li, Liu, Wang, Ye. CausalArena: Benchmarking Causal Discovery in the Foundation Model Era. arXiv 2609.11897, 2026
claims.claim: CausalArena is a benchmark of synthetic, semantic (named, story-based) and formula-grounded structural causal models with observational and interventional exports and a public leaderboard of causal-discovery methods.

claims.ref: Chevalley, Roohani, Mehrjou, Leskovec, Schwab. A large-scale benchmark for network inference from single-cell perturbation data. Communications Biology 8, 412, 2025 (arXiv 2210.17283)
claims.claim: CausalBench evaluates gene-network inference on genome-scale Perturb-seq data from the K562 and RPE1 cell lines, scoring predicted edges on held-out interventional data with a mean Wasserstein distance and a false omission rate.

claims.ref: Replogle et al. Mapping information-rich genotype-phenotype landscapes with genome-scale Perturb-seq. Cell 185(14), 2022
claims.claim: The CausalBench data come from genome-scale CRISPRi Perturb-seq screens.

claims.ref: Kiciman, Ness, Sharma, Tan. Causal Reasoning and Large Language Models: Opening a New Frontier for Causality. arXiv 2305.00050 (TMLR 2024?)
claims.claim: Large language models answer pairwise causal-direction questions about named variables with high accuracy on existing benchmarks, and part of that benchmark is memorised by the models.

claims.ref: Long, Piche, Zantedeschi, Schuster, Drouin. Causal Discovery with Language Models as Imperfect Experts. arXiv 2307.02390, 2023
claims.claim: Treating a language model as an imperfect expert gives a guarantee that the true graph stays in the returned set of graphs only under an assumed expert-error model, and the authors' own language-model experiment violated that model.

claims.ref: Vashishtha, Reddy, Kumar, Bachu, Balasubramanian, Sharma. Causal Order: The Key to Leveraging Imperfect Experts in Causal Inference. arXiv 2310.15117 (ICLR 2025?)
claims.claim: Pairwise edge questions to an expert confuse direct with indirect causation; the authors propose eliciting a causal order instead, which is then used together with a discovery algorithm such as PC.

claims.ref: Zecevic, Willig, Dhami, Kersting. Causal Parrots: Large Language Models May Talk Causality But Are Not Causal. TMLR 2023 (arXiv 2308.13067)
claims.claim: Language models may repeat causal facts found in their training text without performing causal inference.

claims.ref: Srivastava et al. arXiv 2510.16530, 2025 (title to confirm)
claims.claim: Language models reconstruct well-known benchmark graphs (bnlearn networks) from the variable names alone, but not graphs published after their training cutoff.

claims.ref: Dong, Liu, Aloui, Tarokh, Carlson. CARE. arXiv 2511.16016, 2025 (title to confirm)
claims.claim: CARE evaluates language models on causal discovery with original, anonymised and permuted variable names (names moved onto the wrong columns while the data are unchanged), and the models' accuracy collapses under the permuted names.

claims.ref: Kitson, Constantinou. LLM-Augmented Causal Discovery: Probabilistic Fusion of Edge Existence and Orientation. arXiv 2608.27472, 2026
claims.claim: Fusing per-pair probabilities from a language model and from data with obfuscated variable names, the authors note that benchmark recognition cannot be ruled out.

claims.ref: Li, Russo. UAI 2026, PMLR 337 (arXiv 2602.16481; title to confirm)
claims.claim: Language-model constraints are kept only when repeated queries agree and enter as defeasible assumptions that data can override, and the evaluation uses random graphs mapped onto real concept names (CauseNet) to resist memorisation.

claims.ref: Wang et al. Causal-Copilot: An Autonomous Causal Analysis Agent. arXiv 2504.13263, 2025
claims.claim: Causal-Copilot is an LLM agent that runs causal analysis end to end: it inspects the data, selects and configures an algorithm, refines the graph with bootstrap statistics and LLM review, and writes a report; the paper states that LLM recommendations are treated as soft suggestions and are not permitted to override high-confidence decisions.

claims.ref: MATMCD, arXiv 2412.13667 (authors and title to confirm)
claims.claim: MATMCD uses multiple LLM agents with tools to supply constraints to a data-driven discovery algorithm, and reports gains over the algorithm alone on named benchmarks.

claims.ref: Khatibi, Abbasian, Yang, Azimi, Rahmani. ALCM: Autonomous LLM-Augmented Causal Discovery Framework. arXiv 2405.01744, 2024
claims.claim: ALCM refines a data-driven graph with an LLM and reports improvement over PC on named benchmark networks.

claims.ref: Abdulaal et al. Causal Modelling Agents: Causal Graph Discovery through Synergising Metadata- and Data-driven Reasoning. ICLR 2024
claims.claim: Causal Modelling Agents let an LLM propose a graph from metadata and amend it in a loop with a data-driven model.

claims.ref: Tagliapietra, Marchioni, Willig, Luettin, Halilaj, Kersting. CausalSteward. arXiv 2607.01936, 2026
claims.claim: CausalSteward evaluates Causal-Copilot as a baseline on high-dimensional datasets and reports that Causal-Copilot had to be steered towards XGES because it often preferred intractable methods such as FCI.

claims.ref: Zheng, Verma, Gill, Dai, Spirtes, Zhang. Causal Discovery in the Era of Agents. arXiv 2606.23608, 2026
claims.claim: A position paper argues that agents should not supply edges, orientations, priors, constraints or causal conclusions, and calls for audit trails that separate data, assumptions, agent recommendations, user decisions and algorithmic outputs.

claims.ref: causaliq-knowledge, GitHub repository https://github.com/causaliq/causaliq-knowledge
claims.claim: causaliq-knowledge is an open-source package that queries LLMs for causal knowledge about named variables.

claims.ref: PyWhy-LLM, GitHub repository https://github.com/py-why/pywhy-llm
claims.claim: PyWhy-LLM is an experimental library of LLM suggesters for causal modelling, identification and validation in the PyWhy ecosystem.

claims.ref: Mehta. When Agents Disagree With Themselves: Behavioral Consistency as an Uncertainty Signal for LLM Agents. arXiv 2602.11619, 2026
claims.claim: LLM agents give different answers and action sequences across repeated runs of the same task, so single-run evaluations can misrank systems.

claims.ref: Friedman, Goldszmidt, Wyner. Data Analysis with Bayesian Networks: A Bootstrap Approach. UAI 1999
claims.claim: Bootstrap resampling gives confidence measures for features of a learned network structure, such as the presence of an edge.

claims.ref: Kummerfeld, Rix. Simulations evaluating resampling methods for causal discovery: ensemble performance and calibration. arXiv 1910.02047, 2019
claims.claim: Simulations show that bootstrap edge frequencies from causal discovery can be miscalibrated, under- or over-confident depending on the setting.

claims.ref: Banerjee, Andrews, Kummerfeld. arXiv 2503.15436, 2025 (title to confirm)
claims.claim: Plain bootstrap edge frequencies are miscalibrated as edge probabilities, and an adjustment improves their calibration.

claims.ref: Kumar et al. From Causal Plausibility to Causal Reliability. arXiv 2608.23660, 2026
claims.claim: Measured on direct-edge questions, language models' verbalised confidence is poorly calibrated, while agreement across prompts is much better calibrated.

claims.ref: Chen, Cheung, Yiu. Metamorphic testing: a new approach for generating next test cases. HKUST-CS98-01, 1998
claims.claim: Metamorphic testing checks a program without an oracle for each output by checking relations that must hold between the outputs of related inputs.

claims.ref: Segura, Fraser, Sanchez, Ruiz-Cortes. A Survey on Metamorphic Testing. IEEE TSE 42(9), 2016
claims.claim: A survey of metamorphic testing covers its use across many domains, including machine-learning systems.

claims.ref: Ribeiro, Wu, Guestrin, Singh. Beyond Accuracy: Behavioral Testing of NLP Models with CheckList. ACL 2020
claims.claim: CheckList tests NLP models with capability tests including invariance tests (label-preserving perturbations) and finds failures that held-out accuracy hides.

claims.ref: Mitchell et al. Model Cards for Model Reporting. FAT* 2019
claims.claim: Model cards document a trained model's intended use and its evaluation, including results disaggregated across conditions.

claims.ref: Gebru et al. Datasheets for Datasets. Communications of the ACM 64(12), 2021
claims.claim: Datasheets document how a dataset was created, its composition and its intended uses.

claims.ref: Raji et al. Closing the AI Accountability Gap: Defining an End-to-End Framework for Internal Algorithmic Auditing. FAT* 2020
claims.claim: An end-to-end framework for internal algorithmic auditing defines staged audit artefacts that are produced during development.

claims.ref: Moreau, Missier (eds.). PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model. W3C Recommendation, 30 April 2013
claims.claim: PROV-DM is a W3C data model that records the entities, activities and agents involved in producing a piece of data.

claims.ref: Mooij, Peters, Janzing, Zscheischler, Schoelkopf. JMLR 17(32), 2016
claims.claim: The Tuebingen cause-effect pairs include DWD climate data (altitude, longitude, temperature, precipitation, sunshine) from German weather stations.
